themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints in Bed-Stuy spiked to 12 THIS WEEK, up 638% from the 1.6-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.37), signaling a rapid deterioration in street homelessness that aligns with repeated city budget requests for homeless services.
evidence: 12 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (638% spike)
Concurrent spike in Homeless Person Assistance complaints: 10 THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 average (264% increase, z-score: 4.42)
Community Board has filed repeated budget requests for 'Other request for services for the homeless' (DHS), indicating long-standing unmet need
reporting_angles: Ground reporting on specific encampment locations and what triggered the sudden expansion this week
Interview homeless services providers and NYPD about coordination and shelter capacity gaps
Investigate why Bed-Stuy is becoming a concentration point — proximity to transit, services, or permissive enforcement?

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures Surge
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints THIS WEEK reached 13, up 142% from the 5.4-complaint weekly average (z-score: 3.42), likely affecting low-income residents in pre-war walk-ups dependent on aging infrastructure amid ongoing construction.
evidence: 13 elevator complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (142% spike, z-score: 3.42)
847 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (495 alterations), suggesting construction activity may be destabilizing building systems
Concurrent spike in General Construction/Plumbing complaints: 25 THIS WEEK vs. 17.2 average (45% increase)
reporting_angles: Are construction projects impacting electrical or structural systems that support elevators?
Profile elderly and disabled residents in multi-unit buildings waiting for repairs — accessibility crisis angle
Check DOB violation records for which buildings have outstanding elevator maintenance citations

themes_detail.label: Safety Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Safety complaints LAST WEEK jumped to 19, up 198% from the 6.4-complaint weekly average (z-score: 4.33), coinciding with concurrent spikes in encampments, unleashed dogs, and drug activity reports.
evidence: 19 safety complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (198% spike, z-score: 4.33)
Unleashed Dog complaints: 6 LAST WEEK vs. 1.4 average (336% increase, z-score: 3.8)
Drug Activity complaints: 6 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.6 average (269% spike, z-score: 3.59)
Pattern suggests confluence of street-level disorder issues rather than isolated incident
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD about whether they've observed a coordinated increase in calls across these categories
Map the geographic concentration of these complaints — is it one neighborhood corridor or dispersed?
Talk to residents about perceived safety changes and whether they correlate with encampment expansion

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints reached 6 approximately TWO WEEKS AGO, up 269% from the 1.6-complaint weekly average (z-score: 3.59), representing a sustained concern that warrants investigation into open-air markets or distribution patterns.
evidence: 6 drug activity complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (269% spike, z-score: 3.59)
Temporal alignment with encampment spike suggests possible connection between homeless concentration and visible drug sales
Community Board has not prioritized drug enforcement in recent budget requests, indicating either acceptance of status quo or resource constraints
reporting_angles: Are drug complaints clustering in specific blocks, or are they scattered across the district?
Interview community residents and NYPD Narcotics about whether this represents new distribution activity or increased visibility
Investigate whether the encampment spike and drug activity spike are causally linked or coincidental

themes_detail.label: Maintenance Backlog Accelerates
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints LAST WEEK surged to 28, up 239% from the 8.2-complaint weekly average (z-score: 3.9), suggesting deteriorating public facilities amid ongoing construction and potential cuts to city maintenance budgets.
evidence: 28 maintenance/facility complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (239% spike, z-score: 3.9)
Community Board has filed repeated budget requests for DEP (Environmental Protection) and DPR (Parks) other expense and park expansion, indicating ongoing maintenance deficit
Coincides with 847 DOB building permits (495 alterations), suggesting citywide construction disruption may be diverting maintenance crews
reporting_angles: Which facilities are generating the most complaints — parks, schools, NYCHA buildings, or public restrooms?
Interview Parks or DEP about whether maintenance staffing has been reduced or redeployed due to construction activity
Cross-reference maintenance complaints with community board budget requests to show persistent, unmet infrastructure needs
